<description>
Found during #36692: remove test state that is shared and modified across cases.

`tx_mempool_block_doublespend` ran four cases against one chain and mempool, removing each case’s mempool transaction by hand before the next one. Each case is now its own test with a fresh setup that builds the two spends. The first commit also fixes the last case’s comment, which had the mempool and block spends reversed. The checks are unchanged.

The second commit makes the two spends distinct transactions. Previously they were identical (deterministic signing), so in the last case the mempool transaction was removed because it was mined rather than as a conflict. The rejection cases are unaffected: they fail with `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` either way.
</description>

<commits>
07540640aa test: split tx_mempool_block_doublespend into independent test cases

The cases shared one chain and mempool, and had to remove the
transaction each one added to the mempool before the next case.

Give each case its own test with a fresh setup that builds the two
spends, and fix the comment of the last case, which had the mempools and
block spends reversed. The checks are unchanged.

19bb40c987 test: make tx_mempool_block_doublespend spends conflicting

Both spends were built identically and signed with determinitsic nonces,
so they were the same transaction rather than a double-spend. In the
last case, the mempool transaction was therefore removed because it was
mined, not because it conflicted with the block.

Give the spends a different output values so they are actually
conflicting transactions.
</commits>
